svg.data-line-read-by: Claude, 2026-10-31, on the page image: line 2 of the column counted from its top. Every column of the page begins on the same ruled line and no line above this one is blank, so the count is the same whether blank lines are counted or not; Charles Loder's leningrad-codex-tei at commit 15405046fe811d4e1064a7ebcd7cb92261ce72db numbers it line 2 too
svg.data-combined-source: UXLC 2.6, as copied into in/UXLC-39/: Deuteronomy 4:42, atoms 18 to 22 of 22, the whole line; the verse has one cantillation, so the UXLC's text is the combined transcription; Ben has changed nothing in it
svg.data-adjacent-source: UXLC 2.6, as copied into in/UXLC-39/: the line above, line 1, is Deuteronomy 4:42, atoms 14 to 17 of 22; the line below, line 3, is Deuteronomy 4:43, atoms 1 to 4 of 14; the lines' words as Charles Loder's leningrad-codex-tei at commit 15405046fe811d4e1064a7ebcd7cb92261ce72db has them, which the page image agrees with
svg.data-regions-by: Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-01: re-drafted under profile 2 by a script of Claude's from the draft of the same day. Each region's ink is what a watershed on the photograph's luminance gives its seeds: the seeds of the draft's regions that were in one group, those lent to one letter, or to a sign of one written part, joined as one region; and seeds that Claude placed by eye, with the transcription in hand, in written parts that had none and near junctions. The draft's cuts and its regions in two groups are dropped. The groups' ids, kinds, owners and notes, and the supplied ink's reasons, are the draft's, but where a group's note says otherwise; an id sN in them names a stroke of the stroke-SVG. Strips of vellum whose reason says so are proposed by the script, where the boundary between two signs' regions is pale. On 2026-11-02 the region rg84, the top of a letter of line 3, left the qamats g50 for a group of the line below.

path.data-why: Proposed by Claude's script, 2026-11-01, for Ben's review: the boundary between the regions of g17 and g30 is pale here, its paler samples' median luminance 132 against 103, a third of the way from the crop's median of ink, 58, to its median elsewhere, 194.
